text: The UN Secretary General's report of 7 December 1989 states that in the evening of 19 July 1989, some 1,000 Greek Cypriot demonstrators, mostly women, forced their way into the UN buffer zone in the Ayios Kassianos area of Nicosia.
section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

text: The UN Secretary General's report of 7 December 1989 states that a short while later, Turkish-Cypriot police and security forces elements forced their way into the area and apprehended 111 persons, 101 of them women.
section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

text: The UN Secretary General's report of 7 December 1989 states that the Ayios Kassianos school complex is situated in the UN buffer zone, but the Turkish forces claim it to be on their side of the cease-fire line.
section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

text: The UN Secretary General's report of 7 December 1989 states that under working arrangements with UNFICYP, the Turkish-Cypriot security forces had patrolled the Ayios Kassianos school grounds for several years within specific restrictions, and that this patrolling ceased altogether as part of the unmanning agreement implemented in May 1989.
section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

text: The UN Secretary General's report of 7 December 1989 states that in the afternoon of 21 July 1989, some 300 Greek Cypriots gathered at the main entrance to the UN protected area in Nicosia to protest the continuing detention by the Turkish-Cypriot authorities of those apprehended at Ayios Kassianos.
section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

text: The UN Secretary General's report of 7 December 1989 states that the demonstrators, whose number fluctuated between 200 and 2,000, blocked all UN traffic through the main entrance to the UN protected area in Nicosia until 30 July 1989, when the Turkish-Cypriot authorities released the last two detainees.
section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

section_path: C. The UN Secretary General's report

text: Section 70 of the Cypriot Criminal Code defines an unlawful assembly as occurring where five or more persons assemble with intent to commit an offence, or, being assembled with intent to carry out some common purpose, conduct themselves in such a manner as to cause persons in the neighbourhood to fear that the persons so assembled will commit a breach of the peace or will needlessly and without any reasonable occasion provoke other persons to commit a breach of the peace.

Section 70 of the Cypriot Criminal Code provides that it is immaterial that the original assembly was lawful if, being assembled, the persons conduct themselves with a common purpose in such a manner as to cause fear of a breach of the peace.

Section 70 of the Cypriot Criminal Code provides that when an unlawful assembly has begun to execute its purpose by a breach of the peace and to the terror of the public, the assembly is called a riot and the persons assembled are said to be riotously assembled.
According to section 71 of the Cypriot Criminal Code, any person who takes part in an unlawful assembly is guilty of a misdemeanour and liable to imprisonment for one year.

Section 80 of the Cypriot Criminal Code provides that any person who carries in public without lawful occasion any offensive arm or weapon in such a manner as to cause terror to any person is guilty of a misdemeanour, liable to imprisonment for two years, and his arms or weapons shall be forfeited.
According to section 82 of the Cypriot Criminal Code, it is an offence to carry a knife outside the home.

Chapter 155, section 14(1)(b) of the Cypriot Criminal Procedure Law states that any police officer may, without warrant, arrest any person who commits in his presence any offence punishable with imprisonment.

text: Chapter 155, section 14(1)(c) of the Cypriot Criminal Procedure Law states that any police officer may, without warrant, arrest any person who obstructs a police officer while in the execution of his duty.

text: Section 9 of Law No. 5/72 states that any person who enters a prohibited military area without authorization, or by stealth, or fraudulently, shall be tried by a military court in accordance with the Military Offences Act and those found guilty shall be punished.

text: Subsection 12(5) of the Aliens and Immigration Law states that any person who contravenes or fails to observe any of the provisions of subsections (1), (2), (3) or (4) of section 12 shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or to a fine not exceeding one hundred pounds or to both such imprisonment and fine.
